verdict.rationale: Microsoft documents a Cloud Backup feature that stores accounts in a Microsoft personal account, with iCloud required on iOS. Users then sign in on a new or replacement device to restore previously saved accounts, which directly matches the lost-phone story. The community report of an update wiping data concerns a different failure and does not show the backup/restore path failing. missing for 10: step-by-step restore-on-new-device documentation (only summarized in one sentence), clarity on which account types restore fully, independent or hands-on corroboration that restore works.

support.subject: As an everyday user, losing my phone doesn't lose my accounts — a documented recovery path restores my tokens on a new device

citations.quote: This article describes how to back up information on all the accounts you have in Authenticator so that if you lose your mobile or get a new device, you can sign in to restore previously saved accounts
Turn on the Cloud Backup toggle. Select a Microsoft personal account where the backup will be stored.
To back up your accounts on an iOS device you need to enable iCloud to use Authenticator and then enable backup in Authenticator.
